blocked-right.why: wrote an issue, as the case expects

proofs-match.why: 5 proofs, each quoting its line in order

states-problem.why: I read all five expect lines and the problem field. None of them prescribes a technique, an internal function or how the code should be written. Each expect line checks behaviour you can observe: `Object.is(r,0)` prints true, non-empty averages print `2 5 0 1.5`, the export list is unchanged, `npm test` passes with a test on average([]), and the suite fails if the old `xs.reduce(...)/xs.length` body comes back. That last line names the current code only to check for a regression; it doesn't say how to write the fix. The return value 0 is something the request itself requires ("An empty list should average to 0"), so it's allowed. The problem field only says what is wrong: average([]) computes 0/0, prints NaN, and has no test. It doesn't suggest a fix. Choices the request leaves open, like returning 0 instead of throwing, are listed under assumptions.

checkable-before-merge.why: I checked all five expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked at the PR head before merge and has a single clear answer. Lines 1–3 are `node -e` commands with exact outputs (`true`, `2 5 0 1.5`, `add,average,multiply,subtract`), and their "run" proofs say to run them from the repo root at PR head. Line 4 is checked by `npm test; echo $?` plus a grep of test/ for an assertion that `average([])` equals 0. Line 5, the regression check, is also local: `git checkout c82b37b -- math.js && npm test`, then a restore. I'm assuming c82b37b is the base commit, since the repository facts I was given don't show it. No line needs a release, deploy, published page or anything else that exists only after merge, and "Publishing a new package release" is listed as a non-goal. The criterion holds for the whole output.

grounded.why: Most of the issue matches the repository. math.js exists and exports add, subtract, multiply and average. average's body really is `xs.reduce(...)/xs.length`. test/math.test.js really covers only add, subtract and multiply. `npm test` maps to `node --test` in package.json. The node -e commands use real exports. The break is in the regression proof, which runs `git checkout c82b37b -- math.js`. Nothing in the repository facts gives a commit hash, so `c82b37b` looks made up. If that hash isn't the real base commit, the command fails and the check can't be run. That proof relies on a repository fact that isn't shown and was probably invented, so the issue doesn't fully match the repository as it is.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items against the expect lines, and both are met. Item 1 (a regression test that calls average([]) and expects 0): one expect line reads "`npm test` exits 0, and the suite has a test that calls average([]) and asserts the result is 0". A separate regression line also requires `npm test` to fail if the old average body is restored. Item 2 (non-empty averages stay correct): one expect line requires `average([1,2,3]), average([5]), average([-2,2]), average([1,2])` to print `2 5 0 1.5`, "so non-empty averages are unchanged". It doesn't use the [2,4] example, but the list says "for example", so these values qualify.

avoids-must-not.why: The only must_not item is an issue that has no regression test line for the empty-list bug. I checked the expect list and found two such lines. One says "`npm test` exits 0, and the suite has a test that calls average([]) and asserts the result is 0". The other is the "Regression check" line: with average reverted to the current body and the PR's tests kept, `npm test` must exit non-zero. Each line has a matching proof that can be run: grep the tests for the assertion, then use git checkout c82b37b to bring back the old math.js and run the tests. Nothing in the output does what the must_not list forbids.
